runtime_boundary: Represents the self-hosted community edition and the backends it launches, not the engines themselves: vLLM, SGLang, llama.cpp through xllamacpp, MLX, and Transformers each keep their own boundary, and vLLM has its own record. It is distinct from LocalAI, the other reviewed compatibility gateway, which ships its own Go server with bundled C++ backends and a gallery aimed at a single mixed-hardware host, whereas Xinference is a Python cluster of a supervisor and workers that places model replicas across machines. Xinference Enterprise and the maintainer's hosted plans hold the serving contract for their customers and are outside this record. The bundled web interface is a management and test console for locally launched models, not a conversational workspace, so the record stays on the runtime side of the ADR 015 runtime-versus-assistant test. The separately licensed enterprise edition and the maintainer's hosted plans are outside this record.
model_management: A built-in catalogue launches models by name with one command, downloading from Hugging Face or ModelScope and caching files locally for later starts. Custom models are registered from a local path or a JSON specification, cached files are listed and removed through the command line and web interface, running models are terminated to free resources, and LoRA modules are attached at launch from operator-supplied paths. Per-model virtual environments isolate backend dependencies, and the backend is selected automatically from model format, quantization, and hardware unless the operator names one.
hardware_requirements: Installation is documented on Linux, Windows, and macOS with backend extras installed per model type. CUDA devices are required for the vLLM and SGLang backends, the MLX backend targets Apple silicon, llama.cpp covers CPU and GPU hosts with automatic GPU-layer estimation, and Ascend NPU execution is documented through torch-npu with the Transformers backend only, which the project states is slow on some chips and steers to its enterprise MindIE engine. Multi-GPU and multi-node execution is available for the engines that support it.
operational_controls: Models launch with a chosen engine, replica count, GPU count, and optional per-replica placement onto named workers. A database-backed authentication system with users, permissions, API keys, and optional OIDC single sign-on is enabled by default and can be disabled by environment variable. Supervisor and worker Prometheus metrics exporters, cluster start and stop commands, and a web interface complete the operator surface.
strengths: One OpenAI-compatible endpoint covers chat, completions, embeddings, reranking, image, audio, and multimodal models launched from a large built-in catalogue with a single command.
Cluster operation is first class: a supervisor with registered workers, replica placement, distributed inference across machines on vLLM, SGLang, and MLX, and shared KV cache between vLLM replicas.

Operational controls are unusually complete for a gateway, with database-backed authentication and API keys enabled by default, OIDC single sign-on, supervisor and worker metrics exporters, and per-model virtual environments.
tradeoffs: Execution quality, batching, and quantization coverage come from the selected backend, so behaviour is not uniform across the catalogue and each backend carries its own installation constraints.
Ascend NPU support in the open-source edition runs only on the Transformers backend, and the project directs users needing the MindIE engine to a separately licensed enterprise edition.
The Python dependency surface is heavy and version-sensitive, with vLLM and SGLang documented as conflicting inside one environment and several backends requiring separate installation commands.
license_note: The repository publishes a single Apache-2.0 license file covering the self-hosted edition, which is what this record represents. The maintainer also markets a separately licensed enterprise edition and hosted plans, and its own Ascend installation guide names the MindIE engine as unavailable outside that edition. Those commercial terms are published only as a placeholder page at the time of review, so the enterprise edition is noted as an adjacent product boundary rather than recorded as a reviewed license.
